body:
```suggestion
			If [code]true[/code], screen-space contact shadows are enabled. These catch small-scale shadows that shadow maps miss, such as foliage, crevices, and the contact points where objects meet surfaces. Contact shadows are also cast by objects that have their [member GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow] property set to [constant GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF], which can be useful for performance reasons.
```

Would it be possible to keep this variable exclusive to the `is SCSS enabled?` if statement? Otherwise, the SGPR cost is always paid even if the variable is not used.

Maybe you could compute it on CPU and pass it as "scss_slot" in LightData struct, with 0xFFFFFFFF meaning it's disabled.
I think that should work. Will take a loot at implementing it this weekend
This is supposed to be uniform for the entire thread group, right? Just trying to make sure the barriers below do not invoke undefined behavior due to the early return.
Yes, they will evaluate the same for the entire group
Having this as a float parameter feels really unnatural when it's actually a bool value. Anything stopping you from having it as getter/setter functions in light storage?

Would be cool if you could include TAA frame count here like it's already done for directional soft shadows, so it can accumulate and appear softer over time: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl#L323

Fixed.

It seems to overlap a lot with `shadow_contact_shadows_opacity` since they are both about modulating the amount of contrast that the shadows have.
